sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Westchester County
sections.html:
Your city or town collects it, not the county. The Westchester County Tax Commission asks owners not to mail the county checks, because the county takes no property tax payments directly. The 25 cities and towns also bill and collect the county's share, then guarantee and forward the total to the county's Finance Department.

The county covers six cities, 19 towns and 23 villages, with White Plains as the county seat. Yonkers is the largest municipality. Bills, assessment records and tax history all live at the local level, so the first call about a bill goes to the municipality where the house sits.

  • City or town receiver of taxes: bills, payments, balances and payoff letters.
  • Local assessor: value, exemptions and name changes.
  • County Finance Department, 148 Martine Avenue, White Plains: county tax refunds after a small claims reduction. The Commissioner of Finance is also the county treasurer.
  • County Tax Commission, 110 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., Room L-346, White Plains, phone 914-995-4325: general property tax questions and equalization data.

sections.h2: What the County Tax Commission does
sections.html:
Its job is to spread the county levy fairly among the municipalities and to train local assessment staff. Each year it reviews local assessment rolls for that purpose, orients new assessors, trains Board of Assessment Review members and reviews applications to correct tax and assessment errors. It also publishes an annual report on assessments, equalization, exemptions and tax rates.

The Commission sets no individual assessments, collects no current or delinquent tax, and takes no part in lien sales or foreclosure. Those jobs belong to the cities, towns and villages. The county describes its own property taxes as among the highest in the nation, which is one reason local grievance deadlines matter to a seller.

Dates depend on the municipality, and the county publishes a chart of the last day to pay without penalty. County tax is due once a year in April, May or June in most of the cities below, and Peekskill splits it in two. City, town and school bills follow their own calendars, and a village adds a fourth bill in some places.

Yonkers dates shift with the date the City Council sets the levy, and Yonkers pays city and school tax in three installments. For a town or village, use the full chart on the county site or call the local receiver, because those dates differ from town to town.

The city or town where the property sits runs them. The county Finance Department conducts no delinquent property tax lien sales. The cities and towns also pursue collection against owners who fall behind, so a balance that looks old can still be enforced locally.

State law gives the outline for a delinquent parcel. A lien can be redeemed by paying the amount due plus legal charges, and the redemption period under RPTL 1110 ends two years after the lien date unless a notice or a local choice changes it. Legal charges can include notice costs, interest and penalties, and an allowance of up to $250 or 2 percent of the amount due on a parcel, whichever is greater, under RPTL 1102.

Local rules differ. Yonkers charges 15 percent annual interest from the confirmation date with no grace period, and White Plains charges 1 percent a month on overdue tax. Ask the municipality that holds your lien for its sale schedule, and whether any notices have been mailed.

sections.h2: How a small claims reduction becomes a refund
sections.html:
After you win a Small Claim Assessment Review in court, your municipality has to complete a county refund form, and the county aims to process its portion within 90 days after it has all the paperwork. The form needs signatures from the assessor and the receiver of taxes, plus a copy of the court decision or the settlement signed by the hearing officer.

The municipality mails the package to the County Finance Department, Attn: SCAR Processing, 148 Martine Avenue, Suite 724, White Plains, NY 10601. The refund check goes to the owner's address, or to the address on the court order. The county cannot process incomplete paperwork, and it handles only the county portion of the refund. Ask your city, town or school district about refunds of local tax.

The process is meant for residential owners. If you plan to sell, tell the title company about any pending SCAR result and ask who receives a refund that arrives after closing.

The county had an estimated 1,015,743 residents in July 2025. About 61.8 percent of households own their home. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $663,200 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income is $118,976.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $4,000 a month, and median gross rent is $1,951. The county mixes dense cities with large-lot suburbs, so a median value says little about your own street. Look at recent nearby sales.

sections.h2: Selling a Westchester house with tax due
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the city or town receiver of taxes, since that office holds the combined county, local and school figures. Then work through a short list.

  • Find out which installments are paid and which are open, including school tax.
  • Ask whether the bill is on a lien list and whether a sale or redemption deadline is coming.
  • Ask for the exact payoff date that interest runs to.
  • Check whether a Small Claim Assessment Review or a certiorari case is pending on the parcel.
  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address on the assessment roll.

A cash buyer can close with these balances open, and the title company pays them from your proceeds at the table. What you net depends on the payoff amounts, so get them in writing.

Plan the timing too. Ask the receiver which installments will come due between listing and closing, and who will pay them. Because school, city and county bills fall on different months, a closing in the middle of the year can leave one bill paid and another open. Your attorney or title company can split these at the table, but they need the receiver's figures first, and the local receiver is the only office that can supply them.

faqs.q: Do I pay Westchester County property tax to the county?
faqs.a: No. You pay your city or town, which also bills the county's share. The county's Tax Commission asks owners not to mail property tax checks to the county.

faqs.q: Does Westchester County sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. The County Finance Department runs no delinquent tax lien sales. The city or town where the property sits conducts them.

faqs.q: Where do I send paperwork for a Westchester small claims refund?
faqs.a: Your municipality sends it to County Finance, Attn: SCAR Processing, 148 Martine Avenue, Suite 724, White Plains, NY 10601. You do not mail the county form yourself.

faqs.q: How can I find a Westchester city's tax dates?
faqs.a: Use the county's chart of property tax payment dates, which lists the last day to pay without penalty for each municipality. Yonkers dates vary with the City Council's levy date, so confirm with the city's tax office.

faqs.q: Who can answer questions about Westchester equalization rates?
faqs.a: The County Tax Commission in White Plains, phone 914-995-4325. It publishes equalization tables and historical rates, and takes questions about county property taxes and exemptions.
